title: Associated primes of a quotient under flat base change
statement: Let R and S be Noetherian commutative rings, with S a flat R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let I be an ideal of R. Every associated prime q of the S-module S/IS is an associated prime of S/pS for some associated prime p of the R-module R/I [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. Here IS and pS are extensions along the algebra map R -> S, and associated primes use Mathlib's equivalent Noetherian definition.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), specialized to M=R/I and N=S, and proof of Lemma Tag 0330 (lemma-criterion-analytically-unramified), lines 45934-45962, displayed associated-prime formula

proof.text: Identify (R/I) tensor_R S with S/IS as S-modules using Ideal.qoutMapEquivTensorQout and tensor commutation. Transport the S-action on (R/I) tensor_R S along commutation, exactly as in the Bourbaki theorem. Use isAssociatedPrime_iff and the linear equivalence to transfer q into the annihilator-associated-prime set of this tensor product.

Apply the equality clause of annihilatorAssociatedPrimes_flat_base_change [lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-flat-base-change] with M=R/I and N=S. Noetherianity of R gives equality. Membership in the double union supplies p in Ass_R(R/I) and q in Ass_S(S/((p:Set R) smul top)).

The S-submodule (p:Set R) smul top equals the extended ideal pS: each generating scalar product algebraMap(r)*s lies in pS; conversely every algebraMap(r), r in p, lies in the scalar-product submodule by multiplication by one, and the submodule contains their S-span. Rewrite this equality and convert both annihilator memberships back using isAssociatedPrime_iff. Noetherianity of S is used for the latter conversion.

theorem associatedPrimes_quotient_map_of_flat
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Flat R S]
    (I : Ideal R) (q : Ideal S)
    (hq : q ∈ associatedPrimes S (S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S))) :
    ∃ p ∈ associatedPrimes R (R ⧸ I),
      q ∈ associatedPrimes S (S ⧸ p.map (algebraMap R S))
